chunk_findings.detail: The block extraction is unsafe once `text` is the brief. If the first occurrence of `"clitool"` is within the first 400 characters — plausible for volatile brief lines that begin with the companion state — the slice start becomes negative. For example, if the brief begins with `"clitool"` and is longer than 800 characters, `text[-400 : 400]` normalizes to an empty slice (or, for lengths between 400 and 800, skips the text immediately following `"clitool"`). Then `assert "companions_add" not in block` can pass even when `"companions_add"` appears right after `"clitool"`, so the retargeted test no longer proves what its comment claims.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_companion_kinds.py (`block = text[text.index("clitool") - 400 : text.index("clitool") + 400]`)

chunk_findings.detail: The retargeted tests treat `brief_volatile.volatile_lines(...)` as if it returns a single string. In `test_import_real_project.py`, the new code assigns `text = brief_volatile.volatile_lines(_instruction_vars(repo))` and then calls `text.lower()`; the other files in this part (`test_import_verify.py`, `test_onboard_command.py`, `test_rules_surface.py`) also use direct substring checks against that result. `volatile_lines` returns a sequence of brief lines (the same change adds a `_brief_lines` helper in the companion/enforce tests to adapt those lines), so for a repo that triggers the import offer, `text.lower()` raises `AttributeError`, and the plain `assert "..." in text` checks only compare whole list elements rather than substrings. The tests therefore fail instead of pinning the brief content.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_import_real_project.py:text.lower

chunk_findings.detail: The retarget leaves the proof window as `text[text.index("clitool") - 400 : text.index("clitool") + 400]` while switching `text` from the long handshake to `brief_volatile.volatile_lines`. If "clitool" occurs before index 400 (likely: the brief is only the volatile companion lines, so the id is near the start), the start index is negative. Python then normalizes it to `len(text) + (index - 400)`. When that is greater than `index + 400`, the slice is empty. `assert "companions_add" not in block` is then true for every brief, including one that still offers `companions_add` next to "clitool" — the exact vacuous-green failure the comment above this assertion describes. Example: index 80 and any brief longer than 480 characters yields `text[-320:480]`, which is empty whenever `len(text) - 320 > 480`.

chunk_findings.detail: The file retargets the resources seam to `ddflow.adapters.resources`, but it still binds the proc seam to the compatibility shim `ddflow.infra.proc`. Any test in this file that monkeypatches `P.run` (the usual reason this test module imports `P`) therefore patches the shim namespace, not the canonical proc module used by the migrated `ddflow.adapters.resources` adapter. For example, a test that does `monkeypatch.setattr(P, "run", fake_run)` and then calls `R.capture(...)` will not intercept the call to `ddflow.adapters.proc.run`; the fake is bypassed and the test either runs a real subprocess or fails its assertion instead of exercising the intended seam.
